report:
### Conclusion
Current scientific evidence supports the claim that targeted acupuncture can help reduce depression symptoms during pregnancy (antenatal depression).

### Summary of Evidence
* **Clinical Efficacy:** Randomized controlled trials evaluating depression-specific acupuncture against control groups show that targeted acupuncture protocols yield significant symptom reduction. Response rates were found to be comparable to standard depression treatments of similar duration (https://journals.lww.com/greenjournal/Fulltext/2010/03000/Acupuncture_for_Depression_During_Pregnancy__A.7.aspx, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S041564121000072X).
* **Systematic Findings:** Reviews evaluating complementary management for antenatal mood disorders indicate that acupuncture offers a promising pathway for reducing antenatal depression symptoms (https://www.midwife.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Jnl-57-2021-article-3-acupuncture.pdf).
* **Role as Adjunct Care:** Preliminary clinical research highlights acupuncture as a viable non-pharmacological option or adjunct therapy, particularly for pregnant women seeking effective treatments while minimizing potential drug-related risks or side effects (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4758005/).

Although researchers note that the overall number of clinical trials specifically focused on prenatal depression remains somewhat limited, the existing evidence indicates that depression-specific acupuncture is a safe and viable treatment option during pregnancy.
